summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose about 61% YoY to around 550 crores, with PAT up about 38% to around 22 crores; order book stated at 1,755 crores.
summary.overview: B.R.Goyal Infrastructure reported H1 FY27 (half year ended 30 Sep 2026) revenue from operations of around 550 crores versus 342 crores a year earlier, driven by EPC execution and toll collection contracts. EBITDA excluding other income was stated at around 35 crores (figure garbled in transcript) versus 27 crores, with margin of about 6.4% in H1 FY26 and PAT around 22 crores (up about 38%, PAT margin 4.02%). Management said the company secured fresh gross orders of about 1,087 crores in the half, and the order book stood at 1,755 crores, of which about 962 crores is toll collection. Management indicated the company will keep bidding selectively for EPC, toll and PPP/HAM opportunities, with a stated plan to add roughly 700 to 800 crores of EPC orders in FY27.

financial_highlights.value: EPC about 303 crores, toll collection about 274 crores, others about 10-11 crores

segments.name: EPC / construction (roads, buildings, wastewater)
segments.commentary: Revenue of about 303 crores in H1 FY27. Order book of 589 crores for roads, 72 crores for buildings and 132 crores for wastewater. Working capital need about 15-20% and equipment-heavy; management cites ROCE of 15-25%.

segments.name: Toll collection (TCC)
segments.commentary: Revenue of about 274 crores in H1 FY27 and order book of about 962 crores. About 24 toll plazas operated; working capital about 5% and no equipment cost; management cites ROCE around 30% (or 60-70% including leverage effects as stated).

segments.name: RMC (ready-mix concrete, Indore plant)
segments.commentary: Existing plant of 1.8 lakh cubic metres capacity, utilisation about 70% in H1 FY27 per analyst. Management plans a new RMC plant in Indore with 1.8 lakh cubic metre capacity, targeted for H1 FY28.

segments.name: Residential plotting (Indore)
segments.commentary: About 1.6 lakh sq ft of unsold inventory; no new bookings in the current financial year as company has paused sales.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue mix of roughly 50:50 between toll collection and EPC going forward.
Expects order execution of the current 1,755 crore book over 6 to 24 months; H2 FY27 revenue expected similar to H1.
Plans to bid about 5,000 crores of EPC orders in FY27 at a 10-15% strike rate, implying 700-800 crores of new EPC orders; EPC order book expected at 1,000-1,500 crores by 31 March 2027.
Expects growth of 20-30% per year; management said good performance expected in H2.
Expects working capital needs to remain covered by existing limits, with no new bank guarantee or cash credit requirement foreseen for now.
Expects wastewater orders of 300-700 crores; 80-90 crores of wastewater revenue expected in H2 FY27, via JV/strategic partnerships.
capex_capacity: New RMC plant in Indore of 1.8 lakh cubic metres capacity planned; operations targeted in H1 FY28.
Existing RMC plant at around 70% utilisation in H1 FY27 per analyst; management said peak utilisation is around 80-85% given plant age and breakdowns.
Borrowings: 50 crores cash credit limit plus 315 crores bank guarantees (about 365 crores total), plus about 15 crores equipment loans; management sees no new limits needed.
Plans to bid for two to five toll plazas in FY27 (toll selection focus on NHAI TOT/HAM/DOT opportunities); no internal capital exposure limit set.
demand_pricing: Fresh gross orders of about 1,087 crores in H1 FY27, including Bundelkhand Expressway toll collection and O&M from UPEIDA of 377.54 crores over two years.

Six new NHAI toll plazas won: Katpur (Gujarat) 118 crores, Kusnapur (Maharashtra) 39 crores, Jajau (MP) 151 crores, Surapattu (TN) 119 crores, Chillapallu (Telangana) 108 crores, Khambara (Maharashtra) 52 crores.
Management claims toll collection strike rate of about 70% versus 10-15% for EPC bids.
Cost inflation from fuel, bitumen and cement due to a war-related oil price spike; management says price variation clauses in contracts pass through costs and government compensates losses.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue will toll collection contracts contribute in FY27 and FY28, and how do their margins and returns compare with EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 40-50% of toll contract value would be recognised in the near term; toll contracts carry about 5% working capital and no equipment cost, with ROCE about 30%, versus 15-25% for EPC. Management said EBITDA is not directly comparable due to zero depreciation in toll.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue mix between EPC and toll is expected over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly 50% EPC and 50% toll; ETC contract terms are being revised by government, which may slow ETC for the next 1.5-2 years before a positive shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA grow 28% while revenue grew 61%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to faster growth in toll revenue (lower margin comparison) and higher input costs in EPC from fuel, diesel, bitumen and cement price increases due to the war situation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need more borrowing as the order book grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no new bank guarantee or cash credit limits are needed; security bonds have been accepted by central and some state agencies, replacing bank guarantees.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPC bidding pipeline and expected order inflow for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5,000 crores of EPC bids planned for FY27 with 10-15% strike rate, implying 700-800 crores of new EPC wins; EPC order book expected to reach 1,000-1,500 crores by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company entering wastewater and private building segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Wastewater is being entered via strategic partnerships/JVs because the company lacks eligibility for direct bids; expected wastewater orders of 300-700 crores. Private building opportunity in Indore is being pursued through a newly formed team.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (diesel, bitumen, cement) on EPC contracts; reliance on price variation clauses and government compensation.
Slowdown in ETC (electronic toll) contracts as government revises contract terms over the next 1.5-2 years.
Toll collection makes up about half the order book, concentrating revenue in a few NHAI/state toll contracts.
EPC strike rate of 10-15% versus plan to bid about 5,000 crores; execution of the targeted 700-800 crores of new EPC orders.
No PPP/HAM project wins yet despite bids; management is exploring TOT and DOT models.
Residential plotting sales paused with 1.6 lakh sq ft unsold inventory.
Transcript contains several garbled figures (e.g., EBITDA, order inflow, toll plaza count); numbers should be verified against the filed presentation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order visibility, with management stating H2 performance should be decent and the business is on plan. Cautious on ETC contract policy changes and on input cost pressure, which management said is handled through contract clauses. Vague on PPP/HAM progress, where no project wins have yet been secured.
key_quotes: You can expect a good and a decent performance in H2 because our execution, commitment and discipline execution and timeline we are able to achieve something.
So the toll collection contract increases ROCE level reaches 60 to 70 percent.
We will do it with strategic partnership right now.

adds.what: New RMC plant in Indore, 1.8 lakh cubic metres capacity
Two to five toll plazas to be bid for in FY27 (NHAI TOT/HAM/DOT)

growth.why: Management guides 20-25% annual growth (brief also cites 20-30% and H2 similar to H1), backed by a 1,755 crore order book (962 crore toll) with execution over 6-24 months, plus a planned 1.8 lakh cum Indore RMC plant targeted for H1 FY28; the EPC bid pipeline of 700-800 crore is a target, not yet secured.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin looks around 6.4% versus 6.38% a year earlier (garbled figure), with input cost inflation from diesel, bitumen and cement from the oil spike; management relies on price variation clauses and government compensation, which are not yet shown to restore margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New 1.8 lakh cum Indore RMC plant is planned and targeted for H1 FY28 against existing plant utilisation of about 70% (peak 80-85% per management), so it is guided but not yet firmly dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue up about 61% YoY to around 550 crores in H1 FY27 and a 1,755 crore order book (962 crore toll) executing over 6-24 months, with H2 FY27 revenue guided similar to H1; management guides 20-25% annual growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Existing RMC utilisation is about 70% and EPC bidding of 5,000 crores is planned, but no new capex envelope has been announced and management sees no new limits needed (365 crore existing borrowings).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says H2 should be good and the order book gives visibility, but the 20-25% growth guide is only held, not raised, and the EPC order target of 700-800 crores is not yet secured.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include input cost inflation on EPC (fuel, bitumen, cement), a possible ETC slowdown for 1.5-2 years as government revises contract terms, and a 10-15% EPC strike rate against a 5,000 crore bid plan.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launches were discussed; the only new asset is the Indore RMC plant, and wastewater entry is via JVs rather than a new product.

rows.label: EPC order inflow of 700-800 crores in FY27
rows.why: Targeted from a 5,000 crore bid plan at a 10-15% strike rate, with EPC order book expected at 1,000-1,500 crores by 31 March 2027, but not yet secured.

rows.label: Wastewater orders via JV/partnerships
rows.why: Management expects 300-700 crores of wastewater orders and 80-90 crores of wastewater revenue in H2 FY27 via JVs, since the company lacks direct bid eligibility.

rows.label: No new bank limits needed
rows.why: Existing 50 crore cash credit and 315 crore bank guarantees (about 365 crores) are seen as sufficient, with security bonds replacing guarantees, so no fresh borrowing is expected.

tone.note: Management was confident on order visibility, H2 execution and 20-25% growth, and cautious on ETC contract changes and input cost pressure; analysts probed the EBITDA gap versus revenue growth, borrowing needs and the EPC bidding pipeline.
